extracted.intended_audience: creative professionals, agencies and individuals preparing entries for the D&AD Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for submitting creative work to the D&AD Awards and the standards used to distinguish levels of Pencil awards across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefines what's possible in the creative industries
rubrics_metrics.description: Our awards uncover and celebrate truly exceptional work that redefines what’s possible in the creative industries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the overarching standard of work D&AD seeks — entries should demonstrate exceptional thinking that pushes the boundaries of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: A D&AD Pencil equals truly outstanding contributions to creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: A D&AD Pencil is the highest accolade for truly outstanding contributions to creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasises the Pencil as a career-defining accolade; entries are judged to a high standard ('deliberately tough to win').

rubrics_metrics.name: High threshold / deliberately tough to win
rubrics_metrics.description: They are (deliberately) tough to win but easy to enter, with step-by-step support from our team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring note: judges apply a high bar when awarding Pencils; entrants should expect rigorous evaluation even though the entry process is supported and accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wood Pencil
rubrics_metrics.description: For the best of the year in advertising, design, craft, culture and impact. This door-opening honour often represents work that would win the top award at other shows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positioned as recognition for the year's best across core disciplines; useful for entrants to understand relative placement vs. other awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphite Pencil
rubrics_metrics.description: For stand-out work that rises above the rest, worthy of consideration for a Yellow Pencil. This award is a mark of true creative brilliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a higher level than Wood — work should clearly stand out and show creative brilliance to be considered for Graphite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Yellow Pencil
rubrics_metrics.description: For outstanding work that achieves true creative excellence. The career-defining Yellow Pencil commands deep industry respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents 'true creative excellence' — entrants should aim for originality, craft and impact that place work at the top of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Pencil (Impact / Sustained Impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: For exceptional projects that use the power of creativity to drive behavioural, environmental, societal or policy change. Replaces the Yellow Pencil in the Impact and Sustained Impact categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries for Impact and Sustained Impact should demonstrate measurable or clearly argued change (behavioural, environmental, societal or policy). Note: in these categories the White Pencil is the highest recognition (replacing Yellow).

rubrics_metrics.name: Black Pencil
rubrics_metrics.description: For ground-breaking work. Only a handful of these are awarded each year, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the rarest, most revolutionary work — entrants should only expect this for genuinely category-defining, ground-breaking creativity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category-specific expert judging
rubrics_metrics.description: The D&AD Awards have grown this year to incorporate 46 categories, judged by a cohort of over 300 of the world’s leading creatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is carried out by discipline- and category-specific panels (see 'Meet all the 2026 Judges'); entrants should target criteria valued by peers in their discipline and review available category-specific guidance/webinars.
